ann_30.text: This part reads only chest pain type.
Through it, non-anginal chest pain slightly lowers a typical patient's predicted risk, from about 30% to about 27% (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: This part acts on 86 of 242 training patients (36%), patients with a normal resting ECG; 26 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 52-year-old man with non-anginal chest pain, a normal resting ECG and a normal thallium scan), it slightly raises the predicted risk, from about 1% to about 3% (on the training data only).

Through it, a higher maximum heart rate clearly lowers the predicted risk, but only if the resting ECG is normal: from 118 to 175 beats per minute it moves a typical patient from about 65% to about 14% with a normal ECG, and leaves it at about 21% otherwise.
More ST depression on exercise clearly raises it, and even more so with a normal resting ECG (from about 25% to about 82%, against about 18% to about 34% otherwise).
More vessels coloured clearly raise it, and even more so if the resting ECG is not normal (from 0 to 2 vessels, about 21% to about 98%, against about 30% to about 94% with a normal ECG).

For patients with a normal resting ECG, ST depression adds to the predicted risk through this part only once it rises above about 1.6 mm, and more vessels lower it here only up to about 1 vessel (on the training data only; the model has little data on the ST depression threshold).

ann_32.text: This part reads only the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy.
Through it, going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 30% to about 87% (on the training data only).

ann_33.text: This part acts on 17 of 242 training patients (7%); 14 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 58-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, 3 vessels coloured, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it changes the predicted risk only slightly, which stays above 99% (on the training data only; the model has little data on this).
Age and the number of vessels change that patient's predicted risk only slightly through this part (on the training data only).

ann_34.text: Through this part, going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 30% to about 87% (on the training data only).
More vessels clearly raise it even more for patients older than 56 years: from about 31% to about 94%, against about 28% to about 76% at 56 years or younger.
Older age (42 to 66 years) on its own changes it only slightly through this part (on the training data only).

ann_35.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (about 2%), non-anginal chest pain (about 5%) or atypical angina (about 13%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 30%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 30% to about 94%, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) from about 25% to about 82%, and a maximum heart rate of 118 rather than 175 beats per minute gives about 65% rather than about 14% (on the training data only).

A flat ST segment raises it to about 77%, a reversible defect or other abnormal thallium result to about 59%, higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) from about 19% to about 49%, and higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg) from about 20% to about 45% (on the training data only).
Being a woman lowers it to about 3%, and older age (42 to 66 years) raises it from about 26% to about 32% (on the training data only).

For two rare categories the model has little data on this: a fixed defect on the thallium scan (15 patients; about 14%) and a downsloping ST segment (17 patients; about 35%), both on the training data only.
The model ignores exercise-induced angina and fasting blood sugar.

ann_30.original: Hypothesis: 1173 = relu(0.049 cp:3 + 1.976) is an always-active affine relay, effectively a bias term. Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation 1.945..2.053, never clipped; line plot corr 1.0; readout -1.414 gives -2.79 constant logit plus -0.069 per SD cp:3 (logit contrib SD 0.069). Mean-ablation AUC 0.9504 vs 0.9508 full: negligible. Supported; this node is a vestigial relay.
ann_30.proposed: A near-constant relay through which non-anginal chest pain slightly lowers the predicted risk.

ann_31.original: Hypothesis: a two-stage ReLU gate. 4375 = relu(1.118 oldpeak - 0.523) is an ST-depression hinge (active 27%). 1801 = relu(1.555 restecg:0 - 0.516 thalach - 1.286 ca + 0.835*4375 - 1.503), readout +1.859, adds risk for patients with a normal resting ECG, few coloured vessels, low max heart rate and ST depression. Evidence (train, n=242): active 35.5% overall; 70% when restecg:0 is normal vs 0.8% when abnormal; active 55% at ca=0, 15% at ca=1, never at ca>=2, so it supplies risk where the direct ca term is negative. Sensitivity restecg:0 0.55, ca 0.46, thalach 0.18, oldpeak 0.08. Largest hidden logit contribution (SD 1.18); mean-ablating it drops AUC 0.951 -> 0.927, removing its ReLU drops it to 0.791. Supported: the main nonlinearity.
ann_31.proposed: A part that acts on patients with a normal resting ECG: through it, a low maximum heart rate and ST depression above about 1.6 mm raise their predicted risk, while more vessels lower it here only up to about 1 vessel.

ann_32.original: Hypothesis: 2245 = relu(0.397 ca + 1.098) and 7562 = relu(1.047*2245 - 0.372) are affine relays of ca (always active). Evidence (train, n=242): both active on 100% of rows; line plot corr 1.0; replacing their ReLUs by identity leaves AUC unchanged (0.9508). Simplified: 2245 = 0.397 ca + 1.098, 7562 = 0.416 ca + 0.778. Supported; they only carry ca into 3196.
ann_32.proposed: A part that reads only the number of vessels coloured; through it, more vessels raise the predicted risk.

ann_33.original: Hypothesis: 5446 = relu(1.009 ca - 0.384 age - 1.525) detects many coloured vessels, with a lower threshold for younger patients. Evidence (train, n=242): active 7% of rows: every ca=3 row and 15% of ca=2 rows (the younger ones), never for ca<=1. Feeds 3196 with weight -2.10, so it caps the ca pathway. Its ReLU is essential (identity -> AUC 0.655); mean-ablation AUC 0.944 vs 0.951. Supported.
ann_33.proposed: A part that acts on 17 patients with many vessels coloured, whose predicted risk is already above 99%; it changes their predictions only slightly.

ann_34.original: Hypothesis: 3196 = relu(0.629*2245 + 0.663*7562 - 2.102*5446 - 0.217) = relu(0.525 ca + 0.989 - 2.102*5446); 5364 = 0.884*3196 + 0.359 is an always-active relay. Together they add 2.379*3196 + 0.444 to the logit: +1.25 logit per SD of ca until the young-high-ca detector fires, then the excess ca is penalised (net -3.80 per SD). This is a saturating, age-modulated ca term, serial composition relay -> subtraction -> relay. Evidence (train, n=242): mean pathway logit by ca level 0:1.89, 1:3.29, 2:4.50, 3:2.25 (non-monotone); 3196 clipped on only 3 rows; sensitivity of 3196 to 5446 is 2.08 vs 0.62/0.65 for the relays. Combined with the direct ca edge (+1.110) the total ca effect peaks at ca=2. Mean-ablating the pathway: AUC 0.951 -> 0.935. Supported, with the caveat that only 12 train rows have ca=3, so the dip rests on little data.
ann_34.proposed: More vessels coloured raise the predicted risk through this part, more so for patients older than 56.

ann_35.original: Hypothesis: additive composition. logit = -0.540 + a 15-term linear model of the inputs (ca +1.110, sex:0 -1.192, slope:2 +1.037, cp:4 +0.916, restecg:0 -0.651, thal:3 -0.611, chol +0.571, thal:6 -0.530, trestbps +0.487, oldpeak +0.354, ...) + three additive patches: cp3_affine_relay (near-constant -2.79), normal_ecg_st_gate (+1.859*1801, extra risk for normal-ECG, low-ca patients with low thalach / ST depression) and ca_age_saturation (+2.38*3196 + 0.44, a ca term that rises to ca=2 and is cut back for ca=3 / younger ca=2 patients). Nine inputs (sex:1, fbs:0, fbs:1, restecg:2, exang:0, exang:1, slope:1, thal:4, thal:7) are unconnected, zero effect. Evidence (train, n=242): AUC 0.951, acc 0.893; logit SD 3.74 of which the direct linear part has SD 3.31; mean-ablating all hidden nodes leaves AUC 0.923, so the patches add 0.028 AUC, mostly the ECG gate (0.951 -> 0.927 alone) and the ca pathway (-> 0.935). SHAP (prob. scale, full train): ca 0.130, slope:2 0.113, sex:0 0.111, cp:4 0.100, thal:3 0.067, oldpeak 0.049; unconnected inputs ~0.001 (estimator noise). Structural and compositional coverage 1.0, single root.
ann_35.proposed: Any chest pain type, being a woman and a higher maximum heart rate lower the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms; more vessels coloured, more ST depression, a flat ST segment, an abnormal thallium result, higher cholesterol, higher resting blood pressure and older age raise it. It ignores exercise-induced angina and fasting blood sugar.

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises a typical patient's predicted risk to about 94%, and being a woman lowers it to about 3% (on the training data only).

A higher maximum heart rate clearly lowers the predicted risk, but only if the resting ECG is normal: for a typical patient, going from 118 to 175 beats per minute moves it from about 65% to about 14% with a normal resting ECG, and leaves it at about 21% otherwise.

More ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal: going from 0 to 2.8 mm moves it from about 25% to about 82% with a normal resting ECG, and from about 18% to about 34% otherwise.

A flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises a typical patient's predicted risk to about 77%, a reversible defect or other abnormal thallium result to about 59%, higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) from about 19% to about 49%, and higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg) from about 20% to about 45% (on the training data only).
The model ignores exercise-induced angina and fasting blood sugar.
